subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In remote sensing and GIS, georeferencing is the process of assigning what to an unreferenced raster image?
options: Assigning real-world coordinates to raster images
Removing atmospheric scattering from optical satellite scenes
Classifying land cover using supervised training samples
Combining multiple images into a single seamless mosaic
solution: Georeferencing: GCPs + polynomial transformation.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In sequence stratigraphy, the systems tracts LST, TST, and HST are recognized by their characteristic what?
options: LST: transgressive retrogradational parasequences backstepping across the exposed shelf edge and lowstand plain
LST (lowstand, basin floor fan + slope fan), TST (transgressive, retrogradational parasequences), HST (highstand, progradational)
HST: retrogradational backstepping of the shoreline facies belts with aggradational parasequence stacking throughout the entire tract
TST: progradational coarsening-upward shoreface parasequences with forced regression at the top of the tract
solution: Sequence: between two unconformities. Parasequence: flooding surface-bound.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquifer has hydraulic conductivity 20 m/day and a hydraulic gradient of 0.01. The Darcy velocity is:
options: 2000 m/day
0.2 m/day
0.4 m/day
20 m/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An isomorphous series in mineralogy refers to minerals that share which common property?
options: Minerals with same structure but different composition (e.g., olivine: forsterite-fayalite)
No series. Mineral composition is always fixed and never varies continuously
Same composition different structure. A single formula yields several distinct minerals
Different composition different structure. No structural link exists between related species
solution: Complete solid solution: olivine (Mg-Fe), plagioclase (Na-Ca), garnet. Limited: pyroxene.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A downward (trough-shaped) fold, with the youngest beds in its core, is a:
options: Dome
Anticline
Horst
Syncline
solution: A syncline sags downward; limbs dip toward the axis and youngest rocks lie in the core.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The D″ layer just above the core-mantle boundary is characterized by which features such as ULVZs and the post-perovskite phase?
options: Outer core. A 200-300 km thick zone of iron alloy resting directly beneath the lower mantle
Inner core. A thin shell of solid iron that generates the Earth's dipole field and completely stops S-waves
~200-300 km thick. ULVZ (ultra-low velocity zones). Post-perovskite phase. Seismic anisotropy
Upper mantle. A shallow zone of partial melt responsible for low-velocity anomalies
solution: D″: thermal boundary layer. Partial melt? LLSVP (large low shear velocity provinces).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: On the Mohs hardness scale, quartz is assigned which hardness value?
solution: Mohs scale: talc(1) to diamond(10). Quartz = 7.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A mineral has passed through 2 half-lives of an isotope whose half-life is 5.73 (in the given time units). Its age is:
solution: Age = number of half-lives × half-life = 2×5.73 = 11.46.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A brownfield site, an abandoned or underused industrial property, must be subjected to what before redevelopment?
options: Environmental assessment before redevelopment
No assessment needed
Only a structural survey of existing buildings
Only a geophysical survey of the basement
solution: Brownfield: formerly developed land, potentially contaminated. Phase I (desk study), Phase II (sampling) required.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) inversion:
options: Treats measured apparent resistivities as the final subsurface image
Converts apparent resistivities with no iterative modelling step
Smooths the data without relating it to a layered earth model
Converts apparent resistivity data to true resistivity model
solution: Inversion: iterative. Minimize difference between observed and modeled. Smoothness constraints.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A hardground in a carbonate sequence represents which synsedimentary diagenetic condition?
options: Synsedimentary cementation (sea floor hardening)
Deep burial diagenesis after complete lithification
Contact metamorphism by an intruding sill
Glacial erosion and striation of bedrock
solution: Hardground: lithified sea floor during sedimentation. Often bored, encrusted. Represents hiatus in deposition.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How is shale, a common fine-grained sedimentary rock, best defined?
options: Carbonate rock composed of microcrystalline calcite mud and lime
Coarse-grained rock composed of well-rounded quartz sand grains
Volcaniclastic rock made of welded glass shards and pumice fragments
Fissile mudrock (splits along bedding planes)
solution: Shale: most abundant sedimentary rock. Low permeability — hydrocarbon source rock.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly describes fault gouge and its occurrence within a brittle fault zone?
options: Fine-grained clay-rich fault rock
Coarse breccia of angular wall-rock fragments
Undeformed sedimentary fill of a graben
Lava flow brecciated during surface eruption
solution: Fault gouge: very fine-grained, clay-rich. Forms in upper crust. Acts as barrier to fluid flow. Important in petroleum geology.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the intermediate volcanic rock composed mainly of plagioclase plus hornblende or pyroxene?
options: Intermediate volcanic (plagioclase + hornblende/pyroxene)
Mafic volcanic rock composed of olivine, pyroxene and calcic plagioclase
Ultramafic volcanic rock consisting chiefly of olivine with minor chromite
Felsic volcanic rock made of quartz, alkali feldspar and minor biotite
solution: Andesite: named after Andes. Common in subduction zone volcanoes.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The garnet-biotite geothermometer estimates temperature on the basis of which exchange reaction?
options: Ti-in-quartz thermometer calibrated for very high-grade metapelites and granulite facies rocks
Calcite-dolomite solvus thermometer used for impure marbles to estimate peak metamorphic temperature
Garnet-clinopyroxene geothermometer applied to eclogite and granulite facies assemblages
Fe-Mg exchange between Grt-Bt. Ferry and Spear (1978). T estimate from K_D = (Fe/Mg)_Grt/(Fe/Mg)_Bt
solution: Garnet-biotite: lnK_D ≈ (C₁)/(T) + C₂. Calibrated experimentally. Pressure from GASP, GRAIL.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In GIS, the buffer analysis tool generates what at a specified distance around points, lines, or polygon features?
options: Zones of specified distance around features
Zones of equal elevation around a reference point
Linear paths between two or more chosen destination points
Grid cells sharing the same thematic attribute value
solution: Buffer: creates zone of distance around features.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Reservoir quality prediction depends mainly on which factors controlling porosity and permeability with depth?
options: Independent of burial depth because porosity is controlled solely by the original grain size of the sand
Depth (porosity loss), mineralogy (Quartz vs lithic), compaction. Contact cement vs pore-filling
Always high because burial never reduces reservoir porosity significantly
No prediction possible because diagenesis is entirely random in all basins
solution: Porosity: sandstone ~0.5%/100m loss. Lithic arenite: rapid compaction. Qtz arenite: deeper potential.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: To which silicate group of minerals does the mineral hornblende belong?
options: Feldspar group (framework silicate mineral)
Mica group (sheet silicate with basal cleavage)
Amphibole group (double chain inosilicate)
Pyroxene group (single chain silicate mineral)
solution: Hornblende — amphibole. 56° and 124° cleavage. Common in andesite.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Bowen's reaction series predicts that the first silicate mineral to crystallize from a cooling basaltic magma is:
options: Muscovite
Olivine
Biotite
Quartz
solution: In the discontinuous series olivine crystallizes first at the highest temperature; quartz last.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal seam covers 5 km², is 5 m thick, with density 1.3 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
options: 65 Mt
25 Mt
solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 5×10⁶ m²×5 m×1.3 t/m³ ≈ 32.5 Mt.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Subduction zone: oceanic plate subducts beneath continental plate creates:
options: Mountain belt formed by collision of two continental masses
Volcanic arc, trench, accretionary prism, back-arc basin
Zone of new oceanic crust formed at a divergent plate boundary
Graben structure produced by continental extension and stretching
solution: Subduction: Andes-type. Ocean-continent. Mariana-type: ocean-ocean. Deep trench, Wadati-Benioff zone.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Core-mantle boundary (D double prime) is:
options: Region of seismic velocity anomalies
A sharp uniform discontinuity
The boundary between crust and mantle
Smooth transition
solution: D double prime: lowermost 200 km. Ultra-low velocity zones.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What characteristics should a good index (guide) fossil possess?
options: Widespread but short-lived in geologic time
Rare and confined to a single basin with an extremely long stratigraphic range
Found in igneous and metamorphic rocks, permitting absolute-age dating of plutons
Geographically restricted to one locality but present in almost every rock formation there
solution: Wide distribution plus a short time range makes a fossil useful for correlation/dating.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the coarse-grained plutonic rock that is the equivalent of basalt?
options: Coarse-grained intrusive rock that is the plutonic equivalent of rhyolite
Fine-grained volcanic rock with the same composition as diorite and tonalite
Medium-grained intrusive rock consisting mainly of quartz and K-feldspar
Coarse-grained equivalent of basalt
solution: Gabbro: plutonic mafic. Plagioclase + pyroxene ± olivine.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Using a simplified proxy where calorific value ≈ 70 × fixed-carbon%, a coal with 70% fixed carbon has a calorific value of about:
options: 9800 kcal/kg
5600 kcal/kg
2450 kcal/kg
4900 kcal/kg
solution: CV ≈ 70 × 70 = 4900 kcal/kg (illustrative proxy).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The theory that the Earth's lithosphere is divided into moving plates is:
options: Isostasy
Catastrophism
Plate tectonics
Uniformitarianism
solution: Plate tectonics explains earthquakes, volcanism and mountain building by plate interactions.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which statement about ore and gangue is correct?
options: Gangue is the high-grade metal-bearing concentrate recovered during smelting
Gangue is the portion of the deposit that carries the recoverable metal value
Gangue is the worthless mineral matter associated with the ore
Ore minerals have no commercial value and are discarded with the waste rock
solution: The ore mineral carries the metal of value; the surrounding gangue is discarded or processed away.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What sequence of events and phases characterise the Himalayan orogeny in the geological record?
options: Silurian continental collision between the Gondwana cratons of India and Africa and the closure of an early ocean
Tethys closure, India-Asia collision (~55 Ma). Three phases: Eo-Himalayan, Neo-Himalayan
Precambrian assembly of the Indian Shield before the opening of the Tethys ocean basin
A single continuous uplift without any break since the Archean era in the whole region
solution: Himalaya: Main Central Thrust (MCT), Main Boundary Thrust (MBT), Main Frontal Thrust (MFT).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which option correctly describes the shape, sediment distribution and setting of an alluvial fan?
options: Flat, low-lying area alongside a river that is inundated during floods
Low ridge of sediment built along the channel bank during flood events
Fan-shaped sediment body deposited where a river enters a standing body of water
Cone-shaped deposit at mountain front. Coarse near apex, fine at toe
solution: Alluvial fan: flash floods, debris flows. Bajada: coalescing fans.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In a normal fault, how does the hanging wall move relative to the footwall, and what is its typical range of dip?
options: Hanging wall moves up relative to the footwall, driven by regional compression
Both blocks slide horizontally with no vertical movement and a near-vertical fault plane
Hanging wall moves down relative to footwall (extension). Dip 45-90°
Footwall drops relative to the hanging wall, with fault plane dipping less than 45°
solution: Normal fault: extensional tectonics. Graben (down-dropped block) and horst (uplifted block).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Core composition: iron-nickel alloy with light elements (S, O, Si):
options: No light elements. The outer core is pure iron with no measurable density deficit
Light elements explain density deficit of outer core (~5-10%) vs pure iron
Only nickel is present, and it fully accounts for the observed density of the outer core
Only pure iron. Nickel and light elements are confined to the mantle and crust
solution: Outer core density ~10% less than pure Fe at core conditions. Light elements: S, O, Si, H.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Banded iron formation records precipitation of what materials, and in which type of environment?
options: Precipitation of iron and silica from seawater
Metamorphic segregation of iron from mafic host rocks
Submarine volcanic eruption of iron-rich lava flows
Biological fixation of iron by ancient photosynthetic organisms
solution: BIF: alternating iron-rich and silica-rich layers. ~2.5-1.8 Ga.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In marine seismic surveying, an air gun source produces what kind of signal in the water?
options: Pressure pulse (bubble oscillation). Tow cable with hydrophones
A continuous tonal sweep emitted while the streamer is being towed astern
Only electromagnetic signals recorded by nodes on the sea floor
Static electric discharge needing no compressed air at the source array
solution: Air gun: compressed air release. Bubble oscillation produces primary pulse. Hydrophone streamer.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The metamorphic aureole is the zone of contact metamorphism that forms around an:
options: Zone of weathering and alteration around an exposed outcrop of rock
Regional zone of high-grade metamorphism across an entire mountain belt
Zone of contact metamorphism around intrusion. Width: meters to km
Zone of shearing and mylonitization adjacent to a major fault plane
solution: Aureole: inner zone (pyroxene hornfels), outer zone (spotted slate).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Regional metamorphism, affecting large areas, is characteristically associated with which tectonic setting?
options: Local heating by magma at shallow depths in narrow contact aureoles
Impact cratering producing coesite and stishovite at the surface
Mountain belt (orogenic). High P/T. Large areas
Hot seawater circulation altering basalts along mid-ocean ridges
solution: Regional: convergent margins. P-T gradient: Barrovian (medium) or Buchan (high T/low P).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Migmatite: partial melting of crust. Leucosome = granitic melt. Melosome (restite) =:
options: Granitic melt that has migrated away from the source region
Volcanic glass quenched rapidly on the seafloor surface
Felsic fraction that crystallized first from the partial melt
Residual solid (depleted in melt components)
solution: Leucosome: felsic melt fraction. Melosome: mafic residue. Melanosome: dark, mafic-rich.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Metamorphic P-T path: clockwise vs counterclockwise:
options: Both clockwise and counterclockwise paths record identical thermal histories
Clockwise: heating followed by exhumation. Counterclockwise: thickening followed by heating
Clockwise: thickening → heating → exhumation. Counterclockwise: heating → thickening
Clockwise: isobaric heating. Counterclockwise: isothermal decompression
solution: Clockwise: typical continental collision. Counterclockwise: magmatic underplating, arc setting.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Amphibolite facies: T = 500-700C. Minerals:
options: Chlorite + epidote + albite + actinolite (greenschist assemblage)
Pyroxene + garnet + plagioclase with no hydrous minerals at all
Hornblende + plagioclase (andesine-labradorite)
Glaucophane + lawsonite + jadeite + aragonite (blueschist assemblage)
solution: Amphibolite: moderate to high grade. Basalt: hornblende + plagioclase. Pelite: garnet + staurolite + kyanite.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A gravity anomaly measured over a body that is denser than its surroundings will be:
options: Positive (measured g higher than regional)
Positive only when the body outcrops at surface
Negative, since dense rocks give a gravity low
Zero, since density never affects gravity
solution: Positive anomaly: dense body attracts. Negative: less dense. Bouguer anomaly corrects for terrain, elevation, latitude.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Mississippi Valley-type Pb-Zn deposits are characteristically hosted in which rock type and formed at what temperature?
options: Magmatic segregation of immiscible sulfide melts in a layered mafic intrusion
Volcanic-hosted exhalative ore accumulated on the ancient seafloor
Porphyry-style stockwork mineralization with a potassic alteration core
Carbonate-hosted. Sphalerite + galena. Low temperature. Not volcanic
solution: MVT: epigenetic, in limestone/dolomite. Solution collapse breccia. Viburnum Trend (Missouri).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The K-Ar dating method, based on ⁴⁰K decaying to ⁴⁰Ar by electron capture, is applicable to which K-bearing minerals?
options: Rb-Sr method applied to whole-rock samples of the igneous body that is being dated, giving model and isochron ages in detail
⁴⁰K → ⁴⁰Ar (electron capture, EC). T½ = 1.25 Ga. For K-bearing minerals (biotite, muscovite, K-feldspar, glauconite)
C-14 method for recently formed organic material and charcoals of a young age
U-Pb method applied to zircon, monazite and titanite crystals of the same rock
solution: K-Ar: argon retention T ~300°C. Closure T different for each mineral. ⁴⁰Ar/³⁹Ar = variant.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A bed drops 20 m over a horizontal distance of 10 m. Its dip angle is about:
solution: dip = tan⁻¹(rise/run) = tan⁻¹(20/10) ≈ 63.4°.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 5% moisture, 20% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (5+20+15) = 60%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The Darcy velocity of groundwater flow through a porous medium is defined as the:
options: Volumetric flow rate per unit cross-sectional area
Actual speed of a water particle moving through the pores
Total discharge divided by the effective porosity of the medium
Ratio of the hydraulic gradient to the hydraulic conductivity
solution: q = Q/A = Ki. Apparent velocity through total area.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly represents the general chemical formula of the mineral tourmaline?
options: (Ca,K,Na,□)(Li,Mg,Fe²⁺,Mn²⁺,Al)₃(Al,Cr,Fe³⁺,V)₆(BO₃)₃Si₆O₁₈(OH)₄
Ca₅(PO₄)₃(F,OH,Cl) — calcium phosphate with fluorine
K(Mg,Fe)₃AlSi₃O₁₀(OH)₂ — hydrous aluminosilicate of the mica group
Mg₃(Si₄O₁₀)(OH)₂ — hydrated magnesium sheet silicate
solution: Tourmaline: complex borosilicate. Wide solid solution. Schorl (Fe), elbaite (Li,Na), dravite (Mg).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly describes the dark coating that forms on rock surfaces in arid regions?
options: Vitreous silica glaze precipitated on rock surfaces by dew and fog
Thin deposit of wind-blown clay smeared across the rock surface
Hard crust of calcium carbonate formed below the soil surface
Mn-Fe oxide coating on rock surfaces in arid environments
solution: Varnish: MnO₂, Fe₂O₃. Dark coating. Used for relative dating. Rock art surfaces.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Sentinel-2 MSI: 13 bands, 10m resolution in visible and NIR. Best for vegetation analysis:
options: Band 8A (NIR narrow, 20m) and Band 5 (red edge, 20m)
Band 11 (SWIR, 20m) and Band 12 (SWIR, 20m)
Band 8 (NIR, 10m) and Band 4 (Red, 10m)
Band 3 (Green, 10m) and Band 2 (Blue, 10m)
solution: Sentinel-2: 10m in B2,B3,B4,B8. 20m in B5-B7,B8A,B11,B12. 60m in B1,B9,B10.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the main purpose of cement grouting in fractured rock, and which types are used?
options: Grout is used only to raise the temperature of the surrounding rock mass before blasting work
Cement grout dissolves fractures and increases rock permeability for drainage
Cement grout → fill fractures, reduce permeability. Consolidation vs curtain grouting
Grouting is confined to muck filling of the excavation after blasting
solution: Grouting: pressure grouting. Water-cement ratio 0.5:1 to 5:1. Lugeon test for permeability.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which ultramafic, potassic rock is the primary source rock for diamonds?
options: Felsic volcanic rock rich in quartz that forms continental flood provinces
Ultramafic potassic rock. Source rock for diamonds
Mafic volcanic rock composed of plagioclase, pyroxene and magnetite
Granitic plutonic rock consisting of quartz, muscovite and alkali feldspar
solution: Kimberlite: diamond-bearing. Pipe-like bodies. South Africa, Siberia.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Himalayan stratigraphy: Tethyan sedimentary sequence:
options: Paleozoic-Mesozoic marine sediments on top of Higher Himalayan Crystalline
Archean gneissic basement forming the core of the Lesser Himalayan belt
Precambrian granite intrusions that cut across the Sub-Himalayan Siwalik belt
Cenozoic volcanic piles interbedded with the Miocene foreland molasse
solution: Tethyan: marine fossiliferous. Folds, thrusts. Overlying Higher Himalayan Crystalline.
